data.why: The repo ships no sample videos and the web UI has no upload endpoint (captures only come from the Pi camera or --simulate placeholder files), so a seed script inserts realistic UK garden-wildlife detections (fox, robin, cat, squirrel, hedgehog, rabbit, dog, plus one unanalyzed/empty case) with bounding boxes directly into data/wildlife.db, backed by placeholder video files in the same plain-text format the app's own simulation mode writes.

goals: Review today's and recent wildlife activity on the dashboard (recent detections, species breakdown, storage usage)
Browse the gallery of motion-triggered and scheduled video detections, filtering by trigger type or animal class
Open a detection to inspect its ML classification (species, confidence, bird species) and annotated bounding-box key frames
Mark notable detections as highlights and review them on the dedicated Highlights page
Check detection trends and animal-type breakdowns on the Statistics page (charts over the last N days)
Trigger an on-demand test capture from the dashboard to see the full capture -> classify -> detect -> store pipeline run live

review.summary: The tree describes this camera-trap dashboard faithfully and covers the gallery, detail, highlight, delete, statistics and test-capture work well, and all ten screens I opened show what their nodes claim. Before filing, it needs nodes for the parts that simulation mode could not show (annotated bounding-box frames, clip playback, timelapses), the test capture in its own setup phase, and a slimmer f3.
